change_reporting.title: Reporting Settings
change_reporting.description:
Configure how this integration delivers data to Home Assistant.

When **Live reporting** is enabled (default), readings are pushed as they arrive from the gateway with sub-second latency.

Turn it off to cache readings and deliver a time-weighted average instead — you'll set the interval on the next screen. This reduces CPU and I/O load for installations with many panels.

data_description.live_reporting: Deliver each reading as it arrives from the gateway (recommended for most setups). Turn this off to set an averaging interval.
data_description.estimate_silent: When an optimizer stops reporting but the rest of its string is producing normally, estimate its power from its usual share of the string, and add the estimated energy to the String and Total devices. Its own sensors always show only what it reported. Turn off to hold its last reported value on the String and Total devices instead.

set_interval.title: Reporting Interval
set_interval.description: Readings are cached and delivered to Home Assistant as a time-weighted average once per interval.

data_description.write_interval: How often (in seconds) to push time-weighted averaged updates to Home Assistant. Range: 5–300. Default: 60 seconds.

change_inverter.title: Inverter Name
change_inverter.description: Device names are built as Tigo [inverter] [string] [module], for example Tigo Master S2 P01. Leave the inverter name blank if you have a single gateway. Existing entity IDs do not change; rename them in Home Assistant if you want them to match.

rename_string.title: Rename String
rename_string.description: Renames the string for all of its modules. The string total keeps its history.

change_stale.title: Stale reading behaviour
change_stale.description: What an optimizer's own live sensors (power, voltages, currents, performance, duty cycle) show when it stops reporting. Energy sensors are never affected, and string and total power always count sleeping optimizers as 0 W and use estimates for silent ones.

data_description.night_action: An optimizer is asleep once the sun is below 10° and it has been quiet for 10 minutes. Zero: live readings read 0, temperature and RSSI keep their last values. Hold: keep the last values.
data_description.silent_action: An optimizer that stays quiet in daylight (usually a weak radio link to the TAP). Unavailable: live readings become unavailable. Hold: keep the last values. Zero: read 0 like at night.
data_description.silent_minutes: How long a daylight dropout lasts before the optimizer counts as silent (5–240). Short dropouts are normal; on one 19-panel installation gaps reached 76 s in production and 171 s at dawn.
